# 2010B Question 1 {.unnumbered}

::: {.exam-question}
## Question {.question-label}

[**Compare and contrast**]{.task-verb} the pharmacokinetics of orally and intravenously administered morphine and oxycodone.
:::

:::: {#answer-structure}

## Suggested Structure

[**Compare and contrast**]{.task-verb} the agents in parallel columns, distinguishing oral from intravenous administration. Connect bioavailability, distribution, metabolism and elimination to dose equivalence, onset, duration and accumulation.

::: {.structure-table}
| Feature | Morphine | Oxycodone |
|---|---|---|
| Oral and Intravenous Dose Equivalence | | |
| Absorption and Bioavailability | | |
| Distribution and Effect-Site Equilibration | | |
| Metabolism and Active Metabolites | | |
| Clearance, Half-Life and Renal Excretion | | |
:::

::::

## Examiner Comments

::: {.examiner-comments}
**26%** of candidates passed this question.

Main Points expected for a Pass:

- Both Morphine & Oxycodone are full- agonist opioid analgesics used peri-operatively
- They both can be administered orally or intravenously
- They are roughly equipotent when administered intravenously but their oral bioavailability differs.
- Morphine has a high hepatic extraction, so Oxycodone is more potent when given orally
- Major differences or similarities in basic pharmacokinetic (PK) parameters such as volume of distribution, clearance, protein binding, metabolism & half-life

Additional Points which attracted higher marks:

- Actual numbers & content for PK parameters such as morphine’s bioavailability being 30% compared to oxycodone which is 50-87%
- Demonstrate an understanding of the role of pKa in ionization & lipid solubility in comparing the 2 drugs.
- Be able to calculate the dose adjustments & relative conversion between the 2 drugs based on their bioavailabilities.
- Be able to discuss accurately volume of distribution & plasma concentration
- Discuss the different pathways of metabolism & clearance
:::
